'''Solomon Jones III''' (born July 16, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He is 6'10" and weighs 235 lb, playing the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions. He played his [[college basketball]] at [[Daytona State College]] for two seasons (2002–2004) and then at the [[University of South Florida]] for another two seasons (2004–2006). He was then selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]].

==Professional career==
As a rookie, he played in 58 games for the Atlanta Hawks. He averaged 3.3 points a game and 2.3 rebounds a game in 11.5 minutes. After three seasons with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], he signed a two-year deal with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4649 Indiana Pacers sign Solomon Jones]</ref>

On January 3, 2012, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]],<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-free-agent-solomon-jones-120103.html | title = CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT SOLOMON JONES | work = NBA.com | date = January 3, 2012 | accessdate = October 21, 2013}}</ref> but he was later waived on February 7.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-waive-jones-120207.html | title = CLIPPERS WAIVE JONES | work = NBA.com | date = February 7, 2012 | accessdate = October 21, 2013}}</ref> On February 15, 2012, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_solomon_jones_2012_02_15.html | title = HORNETS SIGN SOLOMON JONES | work = NBA.com | date = February 15, 2012  | accessdate = October 21, 2013}}</ref> On February 27, 2012, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_solomon_jones2.html | title = HORNETS SIGN SOLOMON JONES | work = NBA.com | date = February 27, 2012 | accessdate = October 21, 2013}}</ref> In September 2012, Jones signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On October 24, 2012, Jones was waived by the Suns.<ref>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Solomon-Jones/Summary/159 Solomon Jones Player Profile – RealGM.com]</ref> In January 2013, he joined the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. On April 12, 2013, Jones signed with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13023 Knicks sign Solomon Jones for rest of season]</ref> He was later waived by the Knicks on April 15, 2013.<ref>[https://twitter.com/NY_KnicksPR/status/323848252271230976 NY KnicksPR]. Twitter. April 15, 2013.</ref><ref>[https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/04/knicks-waive-solomon-jones.html Knicks Waive Solomon Jones]</ref>

In September 2013, he signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-osby-four-others-prepare-camp Magic Sign Osby, Four Others; Prepare for Camp]</ref> On January 4, 2014, he was waived by the Magic.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-solomon-jones | title=Magic Waive Solomon Jones | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=January 4, 2014 | accessdate=January 4, 2013}}</ref>

On February 10, 2014, Jones was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4738364 BayHawks Add Nine-Year NBA Veteran]</ref> On May 8, 2014, he signed with Changsha Bank Guangdong (a.k.a. Dongguan Snowwolf) of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/119249/solomon-jones-signs-in-china.html Solomon Jones signs in China]</ref>

On September 26, 2015, Jones signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-finalize-training-camp-roster BULLS FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Bulls on October 18, 2015.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-english-hansbrough-and-jones BULLS WAIVE ENGLISH, HANSBROUGH AND JONES]</ref> On March 24, 2017, Jones was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/blue-acquires-solomon-jones/|title=Blue Acquires Solomon Jones|work=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2017|accessdate=March 26, 2017}}</ref>

Jones joined Mexican team [[Tijuana Zonkeys]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usbasket.com/Big3/news/623055/Tijuana-adds-Jones-to-their-roster,-ex-Caneros-Del-Este|title=Tijuana adds Jones to their roster, ex Caneros del Este|first=Dimitri|last=Chelidze|work=usbasket.com|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=November 5, 2022}}</ref> His stint was short-lived, as the rest of the season was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], though he returned to the team for the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sintesistv.com.mx/solomon-jones-de-vuelta-con-tijuana-zonkeys/|title=Solomon Jones de vuelta con Tijuana Zonkeys|work=Síntesis TV|first=Jorge|last=Camacho|date=March 25, 2022|access-date=November 5, 2022|language=es}}</ref>

===The Basketball Tournament===
In 2017, Jones participated in [[The Basketball Tournament]] with Tampa Bulls, a team of USF alumni. Jones' team made it to the Sweet 16 where they lost to eventual tournament champion [[Overseas Elite]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/players/solomon-jones |title=Solomon Jones {{!}} The Basketball Tournament |website=thetournament.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313092759/https://thetournament.com/players/solomon-jones |archive-date=2018-03-13}}</ref>
